perspective:
Sara Manuelito’s available information:

- She is Sara Manuelito, a Speech-Language Pathologist and American Indian woman, working at a community health center.
- Shirley Whiteplume is her long-time colleague, a nurse, and close friend; they have worked together for several years.
- They shared a mutual patient who died. Sara attended the patient’s funeral.
- At the funeral, Sara observed Shirley’s somber demeanor and suspected Shirley was deeply affected. Sara told Shirley she knew it was hard and that she had seen how much Shirley cared. Shirley replied that it had been tough and she wondered if more could have been done. Sara said they did everything they could and should remember the good care and joy they brought. Shirley said it was hard to let go.
- During a work coffee break, Sara raised the patient’s treatment decisions. Shirley said she felt responsible and wondered whether pushing for a different approach might have helped. Sara said they made the best decisions with the information they had and that the burden was too heavy to carry alone. Shirley said she appreciated that but found it hard to accept.
- Sara observed Shirley continuing to be reserved and minimally expressive. In a quiet office moment, Sara told Shirley she noticed she was holding back feelings and that it was okay to be open. Shirley said she did not want to seem unprofessional or weak. Sara said showing emotion does not make someone weak and is healthy among friends. Shirley said maybe Sara was right and she would try to be more open.
- Sara later felt her previous confrontation might have been too harsh. She apologized to Shirley. Shirley said it was a bit much but she knew Sara meant well and appreciated the apology. Sara thanked her and offered to be there however needed. Shirley thanked her and said continuing to talk helped.
- Later, Sara noticed Shirley seemed to be doing better. Sara asked how she was feeling. Shirley said she felt better thanks to their talks and Sara’s support. Sara suggested spending more time together outside work. Shirley agreed and suggested planning something for the weekend.

Sara’s own actions include: attending the funeral, speaking with Shirley there, initiating the treatment-discussion conversation, confronting Shirley about holding back feelings, apologizing, offering continued support, and proposing time together outside work. She has access only to Shirley’s statements, her own observations/suspicions, and her own actions—not to Shirley’s hidden private thoughts or unobserved events.
